reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel measurable structure. Let P be a probability measure on E times R such that its pushforward under the first-coordinate projection is the standard centered Gaussian with identity covariance on E. Let p be any real polynomial, and assume that the response coordinate (x,y)->y is square integrable under P, in the MemLp exponent-2 sense. No other restriction on p or on the conditional distribution of the response is assumed.

Define S={v in E:||v||=1}, with its induced Borel sigma algebra. For any measure rho on S define the real-valued function V_rho on all of E by
V_rho(w)=2 integral_{E times R} [(integral_S p(<v,x>) drho(v))-y] p(<w,x>) dP(x,y).
The inner and outer integrals are the actual Bochner integrals with Mathlib total semantics, returning zero if the relevant integrability condition fails. This formula defines V_rho even for measures rho not assumed to be probabilities; the conclusions below quantify only probability measures. The occurrence of either integral in the definition is not an additional integrability assumption or a separate assertion of integrability.

Then both following assertions hold. First, for every probability measure rho on S, V_rho:E->R is C-infinity on the entire ambient space E. The printed smoothness order is the image of the top element of ENat in ENatOmega, meaning infinitely continuously Frechet differentiable, not the analytic order omega.

Second, for every real number R and every natural number n, there exists a finite real constant C>=0 such that, simultaneously for every probability measure rho on S and every w in E satisfying ||w||<=R,
||iteratedFDeriv_R(n,V_rho)(w)|| <= C.
For n>0, this is the continuous n-linear Frechet derivative at w, with its multilinear operator norm. For n=0, the norm of the zero-order derivative is |V_rho(w)|, so the conclusion includes a uniform bound on function values themselves. In every derivative, rho, P and p are held fixed while differentiating the ambient variable w.

The constant C may depend on the fixed space and its structures, the data law P, the polynomial p, the radius R and the derivative order n. Its quantifier comes before rho and w, so it cannot depend on either the chosen sphere probability or the point of the ball. It is not one constant required to work for all radii or derivative orders, and the statement gives no explicit numerical formula or dimension-independent estimate for C. The factor 2 in V_rho is exact. The derivative bound is an ordinary pointwise bound, not an almost-everywhere bound.

R need not be positive. If R<0 the set ||w||<=R is empty and the bound clause is vacuous; if R=0 it concerns w=0. Natural order n=0 is explicitly included. The space may be zero-dimensional; then S is empty, so there is no probability measure on S and both universal assertions over sphere probabilities are vacuous, with the existence of a nonnegative bound still satisfied. No nonempty-sphere or positive-dimension hypothesis is present. The zero polynomial and arbitrary polynomial coefficients are permitted.

The C-infinity statement is a genuine regularity conclusion about V_rho, rather than a conclusion solely about totalized derivative values. Nevertheless, the theorem does not separately assert integrability of each defining integrand, analytic regularity, or a polynomial representation of V_rho. It also gives no continuity or differentiability with respect to rho, no global bound uniform over all w without a fixed radius, and no uniform constant across changing data laws, polynomials, radii or orders. There is no unit-norm requirement on the evaluation point w beyond the ball condition in the bound; only the integration variable v lies on the unit sphere. rho is arbitrary among sphere probability measures, without a density, smoothness, symmetry or moment-normalization assumption. There is no target vector, conditional-mean regression identity, residual independence, coefficient normalization or degree cutoff among the hypotheses.
objects: The finite-dimensional real inner-product space E; probability P on E times R with Gaussian first marginal; arbitrary real polynomial p; norm-one subtype S; measures rho on S; the literal scalar potential V_rho(w)=2 integral[(integral p(<v,x>)drho(v))-y]p(<w,x>)dP; all ambient Frechet derivative orders; radius R, natural derivative order n and an existential real uniform bound C.
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup, real InnerProductSpace, FiniteDimensional, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace structures. P is a probability measure on E times R; p is Polynomial R. S={v:E:||v||=1} has its induced Borel sigma algebra. V is defined for arbitrary measures rho on S and arbitrary ambient w in E. The theorem restricts rho to probability measures. R is any real number, n any natural number including zero, and C is a real number required to be nonnegative. For n>0 the iterated derivative takes values in continuous n-linear real maps from E^n to R, equipped with the multilinear operator norm.
quantifiers: For every E with the listed structures, every probability P whose first marginal equals stdGaussian E, and every p:Polynomial R with square-integrable response under P, define S and V. Conclude the conjunction: (forall rho:Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure rho implies V_rho is C-infinity on E) and (forall R:R, forall n:N, exists C:R, C>=0 and forall rho:Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure rho implies forall w:E, ||w||<=R implies ||iteratedFDeriv_R n V_rho(w)||<=C). In particular C is chosen after R,n and the fixed E,P,p, but before rho,w.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with the Borel measurable structure; P is a probability measure on E times R; map Prod.fst P is stdGaussian E; p is a real polynomial; the second coordinate belongs to MemLp 2 P. For the individual conclusions rho is required to be a probability on S. The derivative bound additionally ranges over w satisfying ||w||<=R. There are no evenness, coefficient normalization, degree cutoff, unit target vector, conditional-expectation, response-input independence, positive-radius, positive-dimension or regularity assumptions on rho.
conclusion: Every probability rho on S gives an ambient C-infinity potential V_rho. For every real radius R and natural order n there is a nonnegative real C bounding the norm of the total n-fold Frechet derivative of V_rho at every w in the ball ||w||<=R, uniformly over all such rho. At order zero this bounds |V_rho(w)|. The smoothness order is C-infinity and not analytic omega.
scopes: Both smoothness and derivative bounds hold for the ambient function E->R. The sphere restriction is on the measure carrier, not on differentiation or the evaluation point. The law rho is held fixed during differentiation. Smoothness is asserted for each probability rho; the derivative bound is uniform over all rho and all w in each specified ball at each specified order. All assertions are pointwise or global smoothness assertions, with no AE quantifier. Integral and iterated derivative notation is total, but the C-infinity clause is an actual regularity conclusion. The theorem does not give a separate Integrable conclusion, an analytic-order assertion, regularity in rho, or a single constant valid for all radii and orders.
constant_dependencies: The potential has the exact prefactor 2. The finite real bound C is existential, nonnegative, and allowed to depend on fixed E, its structures, P,p,R,n. It is uniform in rho and w, and no explicit formula or independence from dimension or data is asserted. Different radii and orders may require different constants. Negative R produces an empty ball; R=0 concerns only zero; n=0 concerns function values. The zero-dimensional case has no sphere probabilities and is vacuous in those quantifiers. No further numerical constant, denominator, factorial normalization or arithmetic truncation appears.
semantic_notes: The literal integral formula retains its nested measure dependence: rho occurs in the inner prediction integral, while P is the measure of the outer data integral. The label y is subtracted before multiplying by the feature at w.
The printed ContDiff order uses the coerced top of ENat. The approved context distinguishes it from the higher analytic omega order, so no real-analyticity claim has been added.
The positive-order norm is a multilinear operator norm, not a coordinatewise maximum, Euclidean tensor norm or squared norm. At order zero it is the absolute value of V_rho(w).

The theorem genuinely proves smoothness in w. Its total integral definitions are not silently treated as separate integrability premises, and no omitted conditional-response or coefficient condition has been imported.
The quantifier order provides uniformity over every sphere probability. It does not fix rho before selecting C, and it does not require one C to cover all orders or radii.
